description.narrative: Overall, the primary results (outcomes and outputs) of GHGAIV will achieve or significantly contribute to increased Dutch public and political support for Development Cooperation (0.7% GNI) and increased, as well as diversified (both ODA and other budgets), investment (0.1% GNI) in global health in low and middle-income countries.

The Netherlands was historically committed to the 0.7% of GNI to ODA target. However, it has seen successive cuts to ODA under the previous three governments under Rutte. The new coalition government, which struck a coalition agreement in 2021 has very modestly reversed this trend by committing an additional €300-500m/year to ODA.
However, much of this funding is slated for in-donor country refugee costs and the war in Ukraine could put pressure to spend even more on refugee costs if there is a significant flow of Ukrainian refugees to the country. Thanks to the increased power of the progressives in this current coalition, the Netherlands has the potential to meaningfully shift its stance toward being more pro-ODA, but the policy environment is tenuous at best. Additionally, the new Minister of International Trade and Development Cooperation is a part of Rutte’s Conservative party and generally more inclined towards trade than development. It will be critical that she is held to account on development by MPs.
However, there are few Dutch MP champions on ODA and global health — CSOs largely rely on very few MPs to ask ministers questions in debates and champion the issues. More MP champions will be necessary to put sufficient pressure on the government to increase its commitment to ODA.

title.narrative: The project integrates climate risks in programming

description.narrative: The integration of climate risks in programming includes an undertaking of concrete actions to reduce and/or mitigate risks related to climate change impact and disaster risks ( for example droughts, erosion, salinization, flooding, etc.) The projects we refer to could be on the themes of health education, justice, security, disaster management, finance and livelihoods.
